title: Mind the elves: why Iceland's roads sometimes take the long way round

words.note: 英式常用祈使句：Mind the step!（小心台阶！）、Mind your head.（小心碰头）。另一个常见意思是“介意”：Do you mind ...?
words.ctx: Mind the elves: why Iceland's roads sometimes take the long way round

ex.en: [[Mind]] the step on your way out.
ex.zh: 出去的时候当心台阶。

ex.en: [[Mind]] your head, the ceiling is low.
ex.zh: 小心碰头，天花板很低。

cloze.after: the elves: why Iceland's roads sometimes take the long way round
cloze.szh: 当心精灵：冰岛的路为什么有时要绕远

words.note: 也说 go the long way round / around。比喻“用麻烦的办法做事”也可以：He always does things the long way round.
words.ctx: Mind the elves: why Iceland's roads sometimes take the long way round

ex.en: The bridge was closed, so we took [[the long way round]].
ex.zh: 桥封了，我们只好绕远路。

ex.en: She walks [[the long way round]] to avoid the busy road.
ex.zh: 她宁可绕远走，避开那条车多的路。

words.note: crew 指一起工作的一群人：a film crew（摄制组）、a cabin crew（机组乘务员）。作集体名词，英式可以接复数动词。
words.ctx: Picture a road crew on the edge of Reykjavik, ready to blast through a field of mossy lava.

ex.en: A [[crew]] of six worked through the night to fix the pipe.
ex.zh: 六个人的队伍连夜抢修水管。

ex.en: The film [[crew]] arrived early to set up the lights.
ex.zh: 摄制组一早就来布置灯光。

cloze.szh: 想象一支修路队站在雷克雅未克的边上，准备炸开一片长满青苔的熔岩地。

words.note: 可以说地点：on the edge of town（在城边上）；也可以比喻快要发生某事：on the edge of tears（快要哭出来）。
words.ctx: Picture a road crew on the edge of Reykjavik, ready to blast through a field of mossy lava.

ex.en: They live [[on the edge of]] a forest.
ex.zh: 他们住在一片森林的边上。

ex.en: The company is [[on the edge of]] collapse.
ex.zh: 这家公司已经濒临倒闭。

words.note: blast 是爆炸、用炸药炸。blast through 也可以比喻“势不可挡地冲过”：The team blasted through the first round.
words.ctx: Picture a road crew on the edge of Reykjavik, ready to blast through a field of mossy lava.

ex.en: Engineers had to [[blast through]] the mountain to build the tunnel.
ex.zh: 工程师得炸开山体才能修隧道。

ex.en: The river [[blasted through]] the old wall after the storm.
ex.zh: 暴风雨过后，河水冲垮了那堵老墙。

words.note: turn up 常带“没预料到”的意味：He turned up late.（他很晚才来）。也有“调大（音量）”的意思：turn up the music。
words.ctx: Before the first charge is set, a group of protesters turns up and asks them to stop.

ex.en: Only five people [[turned up]] for the meeting.
ex.zh: 只有五个人来开会。

ex.en: My lost keys [[turned up]] in the washing machine.
ex.zh: 我丢的钥匙在洗衣机里找到了。

cloze.before: Before the first charge is set, a group of protesters
cloze.after: up and asks them to stop.
cloze.szh: 第一包炸药还没装好，一群抗议者就来了，要求他们停工。

words.note: 不可数名词，常和别的词连用：local lore（当地传说）、folklore（民间传说）、sea lore（航海的老经验）。
words.ctx: Their worry is not the view or the birds, but a large rock that, according to local lore, is home to hidden people.

ex.en: According to local [[lore]], the lake has no bottom.
ex.zh: 按当地的说法，那个湖深不见底。

ex.en: Grandma knows a lot of old kitchen [[lore]].
ex.zh: 奶奶懂很多厨房里的老窍门。

cloze.before: Their worry is not the view or the birds, but a large rock that, according to local
cloze.after: , is home to hidden people.
cloze.szh: 他们担心的不是风景，也不是鸟，而是一块大石头：按当地的传说，那里住着“隐身人”。

words.note: 常用被动：be passed down from generation to generation（一代代传下来）。也说 hand down。
words.ctx: Stories of the huldufólk, or hidden folk, have been passed down in Iceland for centuries.

ex.en: This recipe has been [[passed down]] in our family for years.
ex.zh: 这个菜谱在我们家传了很多年。

ex.en: He [[passed down]] his love of music to his children.
ex.zh: 他把对音乐的热爱传给了孩子们。

cloze.before: Stories of the huldufólk, or hidden folk, have been
cloze.after: down in Iceland for centuries.
cloze.szh: 关于“huldufólk”，也就是“隐身人”的故事，在冰岛已经流传了几百年。

words.note: take offence at sth：因……而不高兴。英式 offence，美式 offense。No offence, but ...（无意冒犯，不过……）很常用。
words.ctx: They are said to look much like humans, to live inside rocks and hills, and to take offence when their homes are disturbed.

ex.en: She [[took offence]] at his joke about her cooking.
ex.zh: 他拿她的厨艺开玩笑，她不高兴了。

ex.en: Please don't [[take offence]]; I was only teasing.
ex.zh: 别生气，我只是开玩笑。

cloze.before: They are said to look much like humans, to live inside rocks and hills, and to take
cloze.after: when their homes are disturbed.
cloze.szh: 据说他们长得和人很像，住在岩石和山丘里，家被打扰时会生气。

words.note: Do not disturb.（请勿打扰）。也可以指弄乱东西：Don't disturb the papers on my desk.
words.ctx: They are said to look much like humans, to live inside rocks and hills, and to take offence when their homes are disturbed.

ex.en: Sorry to [[disturb]] you, but your car is blocking mine.
ex.zh: 抱歉打扰，你的车挡住我的车了。

ex.en: The birds were [[disturbed]] by the noise.
ex.zh: 鸟儿被噪音惊扰了。

cloze.before: They are said to look much like humans, to live inside rocks and hills, and to take offence when their homes are
cloze.szh: 据说他们长得和人很像，住在岩石和山丘里，家被打扰时会生气。

words.note: swear (that) ...：发誓说……。另一个意思是“说脏话”：Don't swear in front of the kids. 过去式 swore，过去分词 sworn。
words.ctx: Few Icelanders will swear that elves exist, yet surprisingly few will rule it out.

ex.en: I [[swear]] I locked the door.
ex.zh: 我发誓我锁门了。

ex.en: He [[swore]] he had never seen her before.
ex.zh: 他发誓以前从没见过她。

cloze.before: Few Icelanders will
cloze.after: that elves exist, yet surprisingly few will rule it out.
cloze.szh: 很少有冰岛人敢打包票说精灵存在，可出人意料的是，也很少有人会断然排除这种可能。

words.note: rule out sth / rule sth out：认为某事不可能、把它排除。Police have not ruled out murder.（警方没有排除谋杀的可能。）
words.ctx: Few Icelanders will swear that elves exist, yet surprisingly few will rule it out.

ex.en: Doctors have [[ruled out]] a broken bone.
ex.zh: 医生已经排除了骨折的可能。

ex.en: We can't [[rule out]] more rain this weekend.
ex.zh: 这个周末再下雨的可能不能排除。

cloze.before: Few Icelanders will swear that elves exist, yet surprisingly few will
cloze.after: it out.
cloze.szh: 很少有冰岛人敢打包票说精灵存在，可出人意料的是，也很少有人会断然排除这种可能。

words.zh: 耸肩（表示不知道或无所谓）
words.note: 可作动词也可作名词：He shrugged. / He gave a shrug. shrug sth off = 对……不在乎、不当回事。
words.ctx: Asked in surveys, many prefer a cautious shrug: better safe than sorry.

ex.en: When I asked where she was, he just [[shrugged]].
ex.zh: 我问她去哪儿了，他只是耸了耸肩。

ex.en: She answered with a [[shrug]] and a smile.
ex.zh: 她耸耸肩，笑了笑，算是回答。

cloze.before: Asked in surveys, many prefer a cautious
cloze.after: : better safe than sorry.
cloze.szh: 在调查中被问到时，很多人选择谨慎地耸耸肩：宁可信其有。

words.zh: 小心总比后悔好、宁可谨慎
words.note: 常用的俗语，可以单独成句：Take an umbrella—better safe than sorry.
words.ctx: Asked in surveys, many prefer a cautious shrug: better safe than sorry.

ex.en: Take a jacket. [[Better safe than sorry]].
ex.zh: 带件外套吧，小心总比后悔好。

ex.en: I checked the oven twice; [[better safe than sorry]].
ex.zh: 我检查了两遍烤箱，小心点没错。

cloze.before: Asked in surveys, many prefer a cautious shrug: better
cloze.after: than sorry.
cloze.szh: 在调查中被问到时，很多人选择谨慎地耸耸肩：宁可信其有。

words.note: be cautious about sth：对……很谨慎。名词 caution（小心），副词 cautiously。
words.ctx: Asked in surveys, many prefer a cautious shrug: better safe than sorry.

ex.en: Be [[cautious]] when you drive in the snow.
ex.zh: 雪天开车要小心。

ex.en: She is [[cautious]] about lending money to friends.
ex.zh: 她借钱给朋友很谨慎。

cloze.before: Asked in surveys, many prefer a
cloze.after: shrug: better safe than sorry.
cloze.szh: 在调查中被问到时，很多人选择谨慎地耸耸肩：宁可信其有。

words.note: shape 作动词，指对事情的发展有决定性影响：Her childhood shaped her views.（童年经历塑造了她的观点。）
words.ctx: Over the years, that caution has shaped real decisions.

ex.en: Books I read as a child [[shaped]] the way I think.
ex.zh: 小时候读的书影响了我思考的方式。

ex.en: Weather [[shapes]] the way people dress.
ex.zh: 天气影响人们的穿着。

cloze.before: Over the years, that caution has
cloze.after: real decisions.
cloze.szh: 这些年来，这份谨慎实实在在地影响了一些决定。

words.note: re-（重新）+ route（路线）。航班、交通、电话都可以 reroute。
words.ctx: Roads have been rerouted to spare elf rocks, and builders have occasionally hired mediators who claim to negotiate with the hidden residents.

ex.en: Traffic was [[rerouted]] because of the marathon.
ex.zh: 因为马拉松，交通改道了。

ex.en: Our flight was [[rerouted]] to another airport.
ex.zh: 我们的航班改飞了另一个机场。

cloze.before: Roads have been

words.zh: 使免受（伤害）；饶过；抽出（时间）
words.note: spare sb/sth：让……免受损失。另一个常用意思是“抽出”：Can you spare five minutes?
words.ctx: Roads have been rerouted to spare elf rocks, and builders have occasionally hired mediators who claim to negotiate with the hidden residents.

ex.en: The fire [[spared]] the old church.
ex.zh: 大火没有烧到那座老教堂。

ex.en: Can you [[spare]] a few minutes to help me?
ex.zh: 你能抽几分钟帮我一下吗？

words.note: 比 sometimes 更少一些。形容词 occasional：an occasional visitor（偶尔来的客人）。
words.ctx: Roads have been rerouted to spare elf rocks, and builders have occasionally hired mediators who claim to negotiate with the hidden residents.

ex.en: We [[occasionally]] eat out on Fridays.
ex.zh: 我们偶尔周五出去吃饭。

ex.en: He [[occasionally]] forgets his keys.
ex.zh: 他偶尔会忘带钥匙。

words.note: 动词 mediate（调解），名词 mediation（调解）。常指在争执双方之间帮忙谈判的人。
words.ctx: Roads have been rerouted to spare elf rocks, and builders have occasionally hired mediators who claim to negotiate with the hidden residents.

ex.en: A [[mediator]] helped the two sides reach a deal.
ex.zh: 一位调解人帮双方达成了协议。

ex.en: Teachers often act as [[mediators]] in playground fights.
ex.zh: 操场上吵架时，老师常充当调解人。

words.note: The car broke down on the motorway.（车在高速上抛锚了。）说人时是情绪崩溃：She broke down in tears. 名词 breakdown。
words.ctx: When machines break down or workers fall ill on a site, someone usually jokes that the elves are behind it, and only half of them are joking.

ex.en: Our car [[broke down]] in the middle of nowhere.
ex.zh: 我们的车在荒郊野外抛锚了。

ex.en: The printer [[breaks down]] every Monday.
ex.zh: 打印机每周一都坏。

cloze.before: When machines
cloze.after: down or workers fall ill on a site, someone usually jokes that the elves are behind it, and only half of them are joking.
cloze.szh: 工地上机器出故障、工人生病时，总有人开玩笑说是精灵在捣鬼，而说这话的人里，只有一半是在开玩笑。

words.note: fall + 形容词表示进入某种状态：fall ill, fall asleep, fall silent。fall ill 比 get sick 正式一点，英式常用。
words.ctx: When machines break down or workers fall ill on a site, someone usually jokes that the elves are behind it, and only half of them are joking.

ex.en: He [[fell ill]] the day before the exam.
ex.zh: 他考试前一天病倒了。

ex.en: Many children [[fall ill]] in winter.
ex.zh: 很多孩子冬天会生病。

words.zh: 是……的幕后原因、在背后操纵
words.note: Who is behind this? = 这是谁干的？/ 谁在背后指使？
words.ctx: When machines break down or workers fall ill on a site, someone usually jokes that the elves are behind it, and only half of them are joking.

ex.en: Police think a local gang [[is behind]] the thefts.
ex.zh: 警方认为这几起盗窃是当地一个团伙干的。

ex.en: I wonder who [[was behind]] the prank.
ex.zh: 我想知道这个恶作剧是谁干的。

words.note: 比 rock、stone 更大，一般指自然形成、表面圆滑的大石头。bouldering 是不用绳索的抱石攀岩。
words.ctx: In one well-known case, a boulder was lifted out of a road's path and set down a safe distance away, by agreement with all sides.

ex.en: A huge [[boulder]] rolled onto the road.
ex.zh: 一块巨石滚到了路上。

ex.en: The children climbed onto a [[boulder]] by the river.
ex.zh: 孩子们爬上了河边的一块大石头。

cloze.before: In one well-known case, a
cloze.after: was lifted out of a road's path and set down a safe distance away, by agreement with all sides.
cloze.szh: 在一个很有名的例子里，经过各方同意，一块巨石被从道路要经过的地方吊起，挪到一个安全的距离外放下。

words.note: by mutual agreement：经双方同意。动词 agree，名词 agreement（协议、同意）。
words.ctx: In one well-known case, a boulder was lifted out of a road's path and set down a safe distance away, by agreement with all sides.

ex.en: The meeting was moved to Friday [[by agreement]].
ex.zh: 经大家同意，会议改到了周五。

ex.en: They ended the contract [[by mutual agreement]].
ex.zh: 双方协商一致，终止了合同。

words.note: 英式 sceptic，美式 skeptic。形容词 sceptical：I'm sceptical about it.（我对此表示怀疑。）
words.ctx: Sceptics roll their eyes at such stories.

ex.en: Even the [[sceptics]] were impressed by the result.
ex.zh: 连怀疑的人都对结果印象深刻。

ex.en: I was a [[sceptic]] until I tried it myself.
ex.zh: 我自己试过之前一直不信。

cloze.after: roll their eyes at such stories.
cloze.szh: 怀疑论者对这类故事只会翻白眼。

words.zh: 翻白眼（表示不屑、不耐烦）
words.note: roll one's eyes at sb/sth。一个很生动的动作描写，常见于口语和小说。
words.ctx: Sceptics roll their eyes at such stories.

ex.en: She [[rolled her eyes]] when he told the same joke again.
ex.zh: 他又讲那个笑话时，她翻了个白眼。

ex.en: Teenagers often [[roll their eyes]] at their parents.
ex.zh: 青少年常对父母翻白眼。

cloze.before: Sceptics
cloze.after: their eyes at such stories.
cloze.szh: 怀疑论者对这类故事只会翻白眼。

words.note: 名词，带连字符。电影里的替身演员也叫 stand-in。动词短语 stand in for sb = 代替某人。
words.ctx: But the elves often serve as a stand-in for something easier to defend: a deep respect for the landscape.

ex.en: The teacher was ill, so a [[stand-in]] took the class.
ex.zh: 老师病了，由代课老师来上课。

ex.en: Who will [[stand in for]] you while you're away?
ex.zh: 你不在的时候谁来替你？

cloze.before: But the elves often serve as a
cloze.after: for something easier to defend: a deep respect for the landscape.
cloze.szh: 可精灵常常是一种替身，代表着更容易站得住脚的东西：对这片土地风貌的深深敬重。

words.note: 指一大片自然或人造的地形景色：a rural landscape（乡村风光）。也可以比喻：the political landscape（政治格局）。
words.ctx: But the elves often serve as a stand-in for something easier to defend: a deep respect for the landscape.

ex.en: The [[landscape]] here is flat and green.
ex.zh: 这里的地貌平坦，一片绿色。

ex.en: She paints mountain [[landscapes]].
ex.zh: 她画山水风景。

cloze.before: But the elves often serve as a stand-in for something easier to defend: a deep respect for the

words.zh: 用推土机推平；强行推进
words.note: bulldozer 是推土机。比喻用法：bulldoze a plan through（强行通过一个计划）。
words.ctx: Iceland's lava fields took thousands of years to form, and once bulldozed they cannot be put back.

ex.en: The old cinema was [[bulldozed]] to make way for flats.
ex.zh: 老电影院被推平，给公寓楼腾地方。

ex.en: They want to [[bulldoze]] the park and build a car park.
ex.zh: 他们想推平公园，修个停车场。

cloze.before: Iceland's lava fields took thousands of years to form, and once
cloze.after: they cannot be put back.
cloze.szh: 冰岛的熔岩地花了几千年才形成，一旦被推土机推平，就再也恢复不了。

words.note: Put it back when you've finished.（用完放回去。）也有“推迟”的意思：The meeting was put back a week.
words.ctx: Iceland's lava fields took thousands of years to form, and once bulldozed they cannot be put back.

ex.en: Please [[put back]] the books when you're done.
ex.zh: 看完请把书放回原处。

ex.en: Once a forest is gone, it's hard to [[put back]].
ex.zh: 森林一旦没了，就很难恢复。

cloze.before: Iceland's lava fields took thousands of years to form, and once bulldozed they cannot be
cloze.after: back.
cloze.szh: 冰岛的熔岩地花了几千年才形成，一旦被推土机推平，就再也恢复不了。

words.zh: 援引、搬出（某种说法来支持自己）
words.note: invoke a law / a name / a memory：援引法律、搬出某人的名字、唤起回忆。比较正式。
words.ctx: Protesters who invoke the hidden folk are often the same people who campaign for nature reserves.

ex.en: He [[invoked]] his right to remain silent.
ex.zh: 他援引了自己保持沉默的权利。

ex.en: Politicians often [[invoke]] history to win support.
ex.zh: 政客常常搬出历史来争取支持。

cloze.before: Protesters who
cloze.after: the hidden folk are often the same people who campaign for nature reserves.
cloze.szh: 搬出“隐身人”来抗议的人，往往也就是那些为建立自然保护区奔走的人。

words.note: campaign 作动词：campaign for / against sth。作名词：an election campaign（竞选活动）。
words.ctx: Protesters who invoke the hidden folk are often the same people who campaign for nature reserves.

ex.en: Parents [[campaigned for]] a safer crossing near the school.
ex.zh: 家长们奔走呼吁在学校附近修一条更安全的人行横道。

ex.en: She has spent years [[campaigning for]] clean water.
ex.zh: 她多年来一直为干净的饮用水奔走。

cloze.before: Protesters who invoke the hidden folk are often the same people who
cloze.after: for nature reserves.
cloze.szh: 搬出“隐身人”来抗议的人，往往也就是那些为建立自然保护区奔走的人。

words.note: reserve 是“保留地”。a wildlife reserve 野生动物保护区。
words.ctx: Protesters who invoke the hidden folk are often the same people who campaign for nature reserves.

ex.en: We saw seals at the [[nature reserve]].
ex.zh: 我们在自然保护区看到了海豹。

ex.en: The marsh became a [[nature reserve]] in 1990.
ex.zh: 这片沼泽在 1990 年成了自然保护区。

cloze.before: Protesters who invoke the hidden folk are often the same people who campaign for nature
cloze.szh: 搬出“隐身人”来抗议的人，往往也就是那些为建立自然保护区奔走的人。

words.note: give sth a second life：让旧东西换个用途继续用，或让被遗忘的东西重新流行。
words.ctx: Tourism has given the legends a second life.

ex.en: The old factory got [[a second life]] as an art centre.
ex.zh: 老工厂改成了艺术中心，重获新生。

ex.en: Repair cafés give broken toasters [[a second life]].
ex.zh: 修理咖啡馆让坏了的烤面包机重新派上用场。

cloze.before: Tourism has given the legends a
cloze.after: life.
cloze.szh: 旅游业让这些传说焕发了第二次生命。

words.note: 比 home、house 正式，常用于书面或法律、历史语境：ancient cave dwellings（古代穴居）。动词 dwell（居住；老想着）。
words.ctx: Visitors can take guided walks through “elf gardens”, buy maps of known dwellings and even stay in hotels that keep a small house outside for their invisible neighbours.

ex.en: The village has about 200 [[dwellings]].
ex.zh: 这个村子大约有两百处住房。

ex.en: Archaeologists found an ancient [[dwelling]] under the field.
ex.zh: 考古学家在田地下发现了一处古代住所。

cloze.before: Visitors can take guided walks through “elf gardens”, buy maps of known
cloze.after: and even stay in hotels that keep a small house outside for their invisible neighbours.
cloze.szh: 游客可以跟着导游逛“精灵花园”，买标出“已知住处”的地图，甚至住进那些在门外专门给隐形邻居留了一座小房子的酒店。

words.zh: 配合、顺着（玩笑或游戏）演下去
words.note: play along with sb/sth。常指明知不是真的，也装作配合。
words.ctx: Locals are happy to play along, partly because it brings in money and also because they enjoy the joke.

ex.en: The kids said they were pirates, so I [[played along]].
ex.zh: 孩子们说自己是海盗，我就顺着演了。

ex.en: He didn't believe her story but decided to [[play along]].
ex.zh: 他不信她的话，但决定先配合着。

cloze.before: Locals are happy to
cloze.after: along, partly because it brings in money and also because they enjoy the joke.
cloze.szh: 当地人很乐意配合，一部分是因为能赚钱，也因为他们自己也觉得好玩。

words.note: partly = in part，部分地。常成对出现：partly because ..., partly because ...。
words.ctx: Locals are happy to play along, partly because it brings in money and also because they enjoy the joke.

ex.en: I stayed home, [[partly because]] it was raining.
ex.zh: 我待在家里，一部分原因是在下雨。

ex.en: The trip was cheap, [[partly because]] we camped.
ex.zh: 这次旅行很便宜，部分原因是我们露营。

cloze.before: Locals are happy to play along,
cloze.after: because it brings in money and also because they enjoy the joke.
cloze.szh: 当地人很乐意配合，一部分是因为能赚钱，也因为他们自己也觉得好玩。

words.note: bring in money / customers / tourists。另一个意思是引进新规定：bring in a new law。
words.ctx: Locals are happy to play along, partly because it brings in money and also because they enjoy the joke.

ex.en: The summer festival [[brings in]] thousands of visitors.
ex.zh: 夏季节日吸引来成千上万的游客。

ex.en: Her café [[brings in]] enough to pay the rent.
ex.zh: 她的咖啡馆赚的钱够付房租。

cloze.before: Locals are happy to play along, partly because it
cloze.after: in money and also because they enjoy the joke.
cloze.szh: 当地人很乐意配合，一部分是因为能赚钱，也因为他们自己也觉得好玩。

words.note: 可以放在句首或句中：I'll go whether or not you come. 也可以拆开：whether you come or not。
words.ctx: Whether or not anyone believes in them, the hidden folk do a useful job.

ex.en: [[Whether or not]] it rains, the match will go ahead.
ex.zh: 不管下不下雨，比赛照常进行。

ex.en: You have to pay [[whether or not]] you use it.
ex.zh: 不管用不用，你都得付钱。

cloze.after: or not anyone believes in them, the hidden folk do a useful job.
cloze.szh: 不管有没有人相信他们，这些隐身人都做了一件有用的事。

words.note: believe in ghosts（相信有鬼）、believe in yourself（相信自己）。believe sb 是“相信某人说的话”，意思不同。
words.ctx: Whether or not anyone believes in them, the hidden folk do a useful job.

ex.en: Do you [[believe in]] ghosts?
ex.zh: 你相信有鬼吗？

ex.en: My coach always [[believed in]] me.
ex.zh: 我的教练一直相信我。

cloze.before: Whether or not anyone
cloze.after: in them, the hidden folk do a useful job.
cloze.szh: 不管有没有人相信他们，这些隐身人都做了一件有用的事。

words.note: 英式口语：I could do with a coffee.（我真想来杯咖啡。）比 need 更委婉、更自然。
words.ctx: Plenty of places could do with a few elves of their own.

ex.en: I [[could do with]] a cup of tea.
ex.zh: 我真想来杯茶。

ex.en: This room [[could do with]] a good clean.
ex.zh: 这房间该好好打扫一下了。

cloze.before: Plenty of places could
cloze.after: with a few elves of their own.
cloze.szh: 很多地方也真该有几个自己的精灵。
